I have farmed my 8 mu of flat land in Quzhou for over fifty years, and at seventy I know exactly what this soil can do. I will stick to the wheat–maize double cropping system that every household on the North China Plain relies on. It is the safest way to feed my family and earn cash, and at my age I am not about to gamble on labor-intensive crops like cotton that need spraying every few days. My high school education means I can read the county extension bulletins and seed labels, so I always sow improved wheat varieties and hybrid maize, but it has never taught me to abandon a proven rotation.

My winter wheat is already in the ground from last October. This spring I will irrigate it three times—at green-up, jointing and grain filling—and top-dress with urea when the wheat greens up. I will spray four times in total: one herbicide, one fungicide and two insecticides. I expect about 500 kg per mu. As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will sow hybrid maize using no-tillage directly into the wheat stubble. That saves my back and catches the summer heat. I will apply compound fertilizer at planting, irrigate twice and spray three times. With the hybrid vigor and timely water, I expect around 580 kg per mu.
